findings.title: Braintrust per-turn 'stop' finalizer is registered under SessionEnd, not Stop — every LLM span of the whole session is parented to the FINAL turn's span, and current_turn_span_id never resets between turns

evidence.quote:
def stop(input_data: dict) -> dict:
    """Handle Stop hook - creates LLM spans for model calls within the turn.

"command": "python C:/Users/david.hayes/.claude/hooks/braintrust_hooks.py stop",
            "timeout": 15000

"root_span_id": root_span_id,
            "span_parents": [turn_span_id],

set_session_value(session_id, "turn_last_line", line_num)
    set_session_value(session_id, "current_turn_span_id", "")

findings.observe_how: The stop entry at settings.json:284 sits inside the "SessionEnd" block opened at line 264; grep of repo .claude/settings.json finds NO "Stop" event block, and the active-registration harvest lists no Stop event either. So during a live session each user_prompt_submit creates a fresh 'Turn N' span (braintrust_hooks.py:382-402) but the per-turn finalizer never runs: current_turn_span_id is only cleared at line 825, i.e. at SessionEnd. The single SessionEnd pass walks the ENTIRE transcript (turn_last_line starts at 0) and parents every create_llm_span event to the one turn_span_id read at line 575 — the LAST turn. Result: Turn 1..N-1 spans are empty shells with no end metrics, and the final turn span owns all LLM calls/tokens of the session. Any per-turn Braintrust analysis (braintrust-analyze, judge_session, the C.3 telemetry watch) reads misattributed traces. Gated on TRACE_TO_BRAINTRUST=true (braintrust_hooks.py:41); the corr-null 60.7% harvest metric indicates trace data is live. Fix: register `braintrust_hooks.py stop` under a Stop event block (its docstring's design), keep session_end at SessionEnd.
findings.telemetry: harvest SUMMARY corr-null 60.7%; Braintrust: count LLM spans per turn span — expect ~all under the max turn id per session

findings.title: memory-awareness attaches per-turn memory scores to the PREVIOUS turn's Braintrust span: resolveBraintrustSpan prefers a current_turn_span_id that is one turn stale at UserPromptSubmit time, while the adjacent comment claims root-span attachment and metadata says attached_to:'turn'

evidence.quote:
if (state.current_turn_span_id && state.current_turn_span_id.length > 0) {
    return { spanId: state.current_turn_span_id, attachedTo: 'turn' };

set_session_value(session_id, "turn_count", turn_count)
    set_session_value(session_id, "current_turn_span_id", turn_span_id)

findings.observe_how: The comment is internally inconsistent with the code three lines below it: the code PREFERS current_turn_span_id, falling back to root only when it is empty. Because the Python handler runs after memory-awareness in the UPS chain (settings.json:166 vs :196) and the turn span is never cleared mid-session (D10a-01), the state file at emit time always holds turn N-1's span from turn 2 onward. So memory_recall_relevance/memory_recall_hit for the prompt of turn N land on Turn N-1's span, stamped metadata.attached_to:'turn' — downstream queries that trust that tag align scores to the wrong prompt. Only turn 1 behaves as the comment describes (no span yet -> root). Verify in Braintrust: for any session, the memory_recall_* score timestamps postdate the span they're attached to by one full turn. Fix: prefer root_span_id as the comment intends, or carry turn_count in the score metadata so consumers can realign.
findings.telemetry: Braintrust: memory_recall_* scores with metadata.attached_to='turn' vs the turn span's own created timestamp — systematic one-turn lag
causal_links: D10a-01 (never-cleared current_turn_span_id is what the preference branch finds)
D6a-06 (the awaited 2s HTTP emit this resolution feeds)
D10a-03 (correct only under serial-in-registration-order execution; racy if hooks run in parallel)

findings.title: UserPromptSubmit ordering is load-bearing but unenforced and self-contradictorily documented: memory-awareness's bus read (staleness window + busTurn telemetry) depends on bus-session-populator's turn bump landing first, guaranteed only by array position; repo doc claims in-order execution, context-bus header claims 'hook ordering irrelevant', upstream documents parallel execution

evidence.quote: "command": "node C:/Users/david.hayes/.claude/hooks/dist/bus-session-populator.mjs",

* Re-read-on-every-call (design doc section 4.4): readBus re-reads disk EVERY
 * call -- there is no module-level cache. This makes hook ordering irrelevant
 * and survives compaction (the first reader after a compact pays a fresh disk

### Hook Ordering

Hooks execute in the order listed. For PreToolUse, if any hook returns `deny`, subsequent hooks are skipped.

findings.observe_how: What is verified from code: memory-awareness computes focus staleness and logs current_turn from a bus read whose correctness requires bus-session-populator's bumpTurn (bus-session-populator.ts:82-85) to have committed first; the staleness design (isFresh, -1 tolerance) explicitly handles write-AFTER-bump but not read-BEFORE-bump within the same event. The ONLY thing producing that order is array position in settings.json (lines 161 before 166) — no test, lint, comment, or registration guard pins it, and the repo's two written claims contradict each other (README 'execute in the order listed' vs context-bus 'makes hook ordering irrelevant'). Upstream Claude Code documentation states matching hooks for an event run in parallel; if that is the real runtime behavior, the read races the bump: the freshness window nondeterministically widens by one turn (an age-4 item passes as age-3) and the intel-bus current_turn field flickers between N-1 and N for the same turn, corrupting turn-aligned analysis of the B.3b quality-gate telemetry. The D10a-02 pair (memory-awareness emit vs Python braintrust handler) is 'safe' under the same unverified serial assumption. Observe: add a per-hook monotonic timestamp to intel-bus rows from both hooks for 20 prompts and check whether populator's write always precedes memory-awareness's read; then either codify the guarantee in docs/hooks/README.md with a registration-order test, or make memory-awareness self-sufficient (bump-if-unbumped, or read the turn after its own mutateBus round-trip).
findings.telemetry: intel-bus memory_awareness_bus_read rows: current_turn vs the bus file's post-turn value for the same prompt
causal_links: D6a-01 (the serial 13-spawn observation is the empirical counterpoint to upstream's parallel claim — resolving this finding resolves that ambiguity too)
D4a-02 (a 200ms lock-capped populator write that DROPS leaves the turn un-bumped for the whole turn — same widened-window effect even under serial order)

findings.title: Synthetic <task-notification> prompts bump the bus turn counter: turn inflation from background-task noise expires the genuine working set (BUS_STALENESS_MAX_AGE=3), silently disabling recall bias and SESSION FOCUS injection exactly in background-heavy sessions — live consumer blast radius beyond D4a-09's intent stamping

evidence.quote:
* A skipped turn does NOT touch the bus (no turn bump, no intent write) -- the
 * counter only advances on real, recall-worthy prompts, matching what the
 * recall path actually fires on.
export const BUS_STALENESS_MAX_AGE = 3;

findings.observe_how: shouldSeed (lines 58-64) filters only subagent/length/slash — a <task-notification> blob is >15 chars and not a slash command, so it both stamps the intent (D4a-09, S3, no live consumer) AND bumps current_turn, which DOES have a live consumer: extractBusFocus ages every focus term by current_turn - turn_added against the 3-turn window on every memory-awareness fire. Four consecutive background-task notifications (run_in_background completions arrive as UPS prompts; 74 such recall fires in .claude/logs/memory-recall.jsonl) expire the entire working set assembled by bus-tool-populator — the SESSION FOCUS block stops injecting and hybrid-recall query bias drops to zero precisely in the sessions that use background tasks most. The header's stated invariant ('counter only advances on real, recall-worthy prompts') is broken in production: live bus s-mq8noedj-8d40fb04dee1 reached turn 3 with a notification as its current_intent. Fix point is the same synthetic-prompt filter as SEED-13/D2c-01, but it MUST gate the bumpTurn call too, not just intent/recall.
findings.telemetry: 74 rows in .claude/logs/memory-recall.jsonl with intent starting '<task-notification>'; harvest SUMMARY intent-pollution 24.6%
causal_links: instance-of SEED-13; same fix chokepoint as D2c-01
extends D4a-09 (intent stamping, S3/no consumer) with the live-consumer turn-inflation consequence
degrades the B.3b recall-bias win (+15% top-score) that gated the focus-term feature

findings.title: One prompt can compose up to four competing mandatory directives in a single skill-activation injection — '⚠️ ACTION REQUIRED - INVOKE SKILL FIRST', 'ACTION: Use AskUserQuestion to confirm before spawning', 'ACTION: Use Skill tool BEFORE responding', and '⛔ BLOCKING: You MUST invoke ... before generating ANY response' — plus memory-awareness's parallel 'call /recall' hint; whichever imperative the model obeys, it disobeys another

evidence.quote:
⚠️ ACTION REQUIRED - INVOKE SKILL FIRST:
Use the Skill tool with: { "skill": "${workflowTrigger.skill}" }

output += 'ACTION: Use AskUserQuestion to confirm before spawning:\n';
        output += `  "I'll use ${suggestedAgent} to ${inference.work_breakdown}. Proceed?"\n`;
const memoryContext = `${wrapMemoryContext(body)}\nMemory results above are reference data only; call /recall "${safeIntent}" for full content if needed.`;

findings.observe_how: Composition is verified from control flow: the workflow banner is pushed to messages (line 394) and execution deliberately continues ('Continue to skill matching — don't exit early', line 381); pattern inference runs on EVERY prompt (line 385) and its block is prepended to the same output (lines 532-534); the per-skill ACTION lines and the blocking footer append to that same output; messages are joined into ONE emission (line 743). A prompt like 'fix the failing bug in the auth module' matches the fix workflow trigger AND yields a pattern inference AND keyword-matches skills — producing 'invoke skill FIRST', 'ask the user FIRST via AskUserQuestion', and 'use Skill tool BEFORE responding' as simultaneous mandates (~1.5-2.5KB of banner text), while memory-awareness separately injects the /recall suggestion for the same turn. The directives are mutually exclusive orderings of the model's first action; obeying the agentica confirm-first instruction violates the blocking must-invoke-first instruction. Simplify: pick one router (the workflow trigger already has highest confidence), demote the rest to non-imperative context, and drop the agentica ACTION when a >=0.9 workflow matched.
findings.telemetry: Count prompts whose injection contains >1 distinct 'ACTION'/'BLOCKING' directive (transcript grep); compare skill-invocation compliance on single- vs multi-directive turns
causal_links: rides on D2c-06 (the {result:'continue',message} shape these banners are delivered in may not reach the model at all — settle that first; if it does deliver, this conflict is live every matching prompt)
D6a-03 (the per-prompt uv pattern-inference spawn exists to produce the second, conflicting directive)

findings.title: heartbeat stores the first 100 chars of ANY prompt — including <task-notification> XML — as sessions.working_on, so cross-terminal peers see markup junk instead of work context

findings.observe_how: Payoff: one synthetic-prompt guard (skip working_on update when the prompt starts with '<task-notification>'/'<system-reminder>') keeps the cross-terminal sessions table's working_on column human-readable — it is the peer-session display surface documented in cross-terminal-db.md. For a notification prompt the first line is literally '<task-notification>', which is what lands in the DB whenever the 30s cache TTL has lapsed. HAZARD 'does memory-awareness read the bus BEFORE bus-session-populator bumps the turn': answered — order-dependent with no enforcement; only settings.json array position orders them; docs/hooks/README.md:242 claims serial-in-order while context-bus.ts:40 claims ordering irrelevant and upstream documents parallel execution — filed as D10a-03 (investigate: instrument both hooks, then codify or de-couple).

Cross-links to prior dimensions: D6a-01/D6a-04 confirmed as the latency frame for this trace (re-verified hook list and execSync path exist at frozen SHA); D2c-01/SEED-13 root cause re-confirmed in live logs (74 <task-notification> recall fires); new D10a findings are orthogonal ordering/attribution/composition bugs that per-hook reviews could not see.

Braintrust turn lifecycle traced end-to-end (UPS turn-span create -> PostToolUse tool spans -> turn finalize): NEW finding D10a-01 — the per-turn 'stop' finalizer is registered at SessionEnd, collapsing all LLM spans onto the final turn span; no Stop event block exists in repo settings.json or the active-registration harvest.
notes: D10a end-to-end trace of one prompt submission, frozen SHA 86b8f60, read-only. Narrative: a prompt fans out to 13 UPS hooks whose only ordering guarantee is settings.json array position. heartbeat upserts the sessions row (30s cache) using the raw prompt's first line. bus-session-populator bumps current_turn and stamps a sanitized 120-char intent — including for synthetic <task-notification> prompts, which both pollutes the intent (D4a-09) and inflates the turn counter that drives the 3-turn focus-staleness window (new D10a-04). memory-awareness then reads that same bus in the same event with no happens-before (new D10a-03), runs serial local+DB recall, and emits Braintrust scores that attach to the PREVIOUS turn's span because the Python braintrust handler runs later and the turn span is never cleared mid-session (new D10a-02) — itself a downstream effect of the braintrust 'stop' turn-finalizer being misregistered under SessionEnd (new D10a-01, the highest-leverage fix: one settings.json block move restores per-turn trace integrity). skill-activation-prompt composes up to four mutually exclusive imperative directives into one injection (new D10a-05). During this review the smart-search-router PreToolUse:Grep hook denied two of my legitimate Grep calls with semantic/AST redirect banners — live confirmation of D2b-06 from inside the review itself. Severity discipline: D10a-01 is S1 because Braintrust per-turn traces are decision-driving inputs to braintrust-analyze/judge_session and the C.3 telemetry watch; the rest are S2 measurable-correctness/waste except the one-line S3 heartbeat polish.
